from qiskit import QuantumCircuit

def build_oracle(qc: QuantumCircuit, problem_qubits: list[int],
                 ancilla_qubits: list[int]) -> None:
    """
    Implements a Grover phase oracle for the 3-SAT instance:
      (NOT x0 OR x4 OR x5)
      (x1 OR NOT x2 OR x4)
      (NOT x0 OR NOT x3 OR NOT x5)
      (NOT x0 OR x1 OR NOT x4)
      (NOT x1 OR x4 OR x5)
      (x0 OR NOT x1 OR x5)
      (NOT x2 OR NOT x3 OR NOT x5)
      (x1 OR NOT x2 OR x5)
    Marks satisfying assignments with phase -1.
    Uses 5 ancilla qubits.
    """
    # Indices: master = anc[0], temp = anc[1], others unused
    master = ancilla_qubits[0]
    temp = ancilla_qubits[1]

    # Clauses: each is list of (var_index, is_negated)
    # is_negated=True means NOT x_i
    clauses = [
        [(0, True), (4, False), (5, False)],  # NOT x0 OR x4 OR x5
        [(1, False), (2, True), (4, False)],  # x1 OR NOT x2 OR x4
        [(0, True), (3, True), (5, True)],    # NOT x0 OR NOT x3 OR NOT x5
        [(0, True), (1, False), (4, True)],   # NOT x0 OR x1 OR NOT x4
        [(1, True), (4, False), (5, False)],  # NOT x1 OR x4 OR x5
        [(0, False), (1, True), (5, False)],  # x0 OR NOT x1 OR x5
        [(2, True), (3, True), (5, True)],    # NOT x2 OR NOT x3 OR NOT x5
        [(1, False), (2, True), (5, False)],  # x1 OR NOT x2 OR x5
    ]

    # Helper to perform one clause computation:
    #   Sets temp = |1> iff clause false (all literals false)
    #   Uses X on problem qubits for positive literals, then MCX, then X again.
    def compute_clause_false(clause):
        flipped = []
        for var, negated in clause:
            if not negated:            # positive literal -> want control on 0
                qc.x(problem_qubits[var])
                flipped.append(problem_qubits[var])
        controls = [problem_qubits[var] for var, _ in clause]
        qc.mcx(controls, temp, mode='v-chain')
        for q in reversed(flipped):
            qc.x(q)

    # ---------- Forward pass ----------
    # Initialize master to |1>
    qc.x(master)

    for clause in clauses:
        compute_clause_false(clause)       # temp = 1 if clause false
        qc.cx(temp, master)                # flip master if clause false
        compute_clause_false(clause)       # uncompute temp (self‑inverse)

    # Mark satisfying assignment
    qc.z(master)

    # ---------- Backward pass (reverse order) ----------
    for clause in reversed(clauses):
        compute_clause_false(clause)       # temp = 1 if clause false
        qc.cx(temp, master)                # undo previous flip
        compute_clause_false(clause)       # uncompute temp

    # Restore master to |0>
    qc.x(master)

        [(0, False), (1, True), (3, True)],    # (x0 OR NOT x1 OR NOT x3)
        [(2, True), (3, False), (4, True)],    # (NOT x2 OR x3 OR NOT x4)
        [(1, True), (2, True), (4, True)],     # (NOT x1 OR NOT x2 OR NOT x4)
        [(0, True), (2, True), (3, True)],     # (NOT x0 OR NOT x2 OR NOT x3)
        [(0, False), (1, True), (3, False)],   # (x0 OR NOT x1 OR x3)
        [(1, False), (3, True), (4, False)],   # (x1 OR NOT x3 OR x4)
        [(1, True), (2, True), (3, False)],    # (NOT x1 OR NOT x2 OR x3)
    ]

    acc = ancilla_qubits[0]      # accumulator qubit (starts |0>, then set to |1>)
    tmp = ancilla_qubits[1]      # temporary qubit for each clause result

    # Initialise accumulator to |1>
    qc.x(acc)

    def compute_clause(clause):

        for var, neg in clause:
            if not neg:  # positive literal -> need to flip for "false" condition
                qc.x(problem_qubits[var])

        qc.mcx([problem_qubits[var] for var, _ in clause], tmp, mode='noancilla')
        # Invert: now tmp = 1 iff clause unsatisfied (all false)
        qc.x(tmp)   # tmp = 1 iff clause satisfied
        # Undo the X gates on problem qubits (reverse order)
        for var, neg in reversed(clause):
            if not neg:
                qc.x(problem_qubits[var])

    # Forward pass: for each clause, evaluate, accumulate into acc, then uncompute
    for clause in clauses:
        compute_clause(clause)               # tmp = clause_result
        # Flip acc if tmp == 0 (i.e., clause unsatisfied)
        qc.x(tmp)
        qc.cx(tmp, acc)
        qc.x(tmp)
        compute_clause(clause)               # uncompute clause (tmp back to |0>)

        qc.x(tmp)
        compute_clause(clause)

    qc.x(acc)

    The oracle applies a phase of -1 to basis states that satisfy all clauses.

    flag = ancilla_qubits[0]

    # is_positive == True  -> literal is x_i
    # is_positive == False -> literal is ¬x_i

        [(1, True), (2, True), (3, False)]     # ( x1 ∨  x2 ∨ ¬x3)
    ]

        # Multi-controlled X: flip flag iff clause is false

def build_oracle(qc: QuantumCircuit, problem_qubits: list[int],
                 ancilla_qubits: list[int]) -> None:
    """
    Grover-style phase oracle for the vertex cover problem.
    Marks states where the set of vertices covers all edges
    and the cover size is at most 4.
    """
    # ancilla assignments
    u = ancilla_qubits[0]      # uncovered flag (1 if any edge uncovered)
    temp_edge = ancilla_qubits[1]   # temporary for edge-pair AND
    w_flag = ancilla_qubits[2]      # weight > 4 flag
    # three ancillas for decomposition of multi-controlled X gates
    mcx_anc = [ancilla_qubits[3], ancilla_qubits[4], ancilla_qubits[5]]
    p = ancilla_qubits[6]           # final phase ancilla (will be Z'd)

    # ========== 1. Compute uncovered flag u ==========
    edges = [(0,2), (0,3), (0,4), (0,5), (1,2), (1,5), (2,4)]
    for i, j in edges:
        # compute temp_edge = (NOT problem[i]) AND (NOT problem[j])
        qc.x(problem_qubits[i])
        qc.x(problem_qubits[j])
        qc.ccx(problem_qubits[i], problem_qubits[j], temp_edge)
        qc.x(problem_qubits[i])
        qc.x(problem_qubits[j])

        qc.cx(temp_edge, u)
        # uncompute temp_edge (block is self-inverse)
        qc.x(problem_qubits[i])
        qc.x(problem_qubits[j])
        qc.ccx(problem_qubits[i], problem_qubits[j], temp_edge)
        qc.x(problem_qubits[i])
        qc.x(problem_qubits[j])

    # Mark states where at least 5 of the 6 problem bits are 1.
    # This is equivalent to OR over all 5-bit subsets.

    # anc[3], anc[4], anc[5] – sum register (LSB, bit1, MSB)

    edge_tmp = anc[1]
    edge_and = anc[2]
    s0, s1, s2 = anc[3], anc[4], anc[5]
    carry1, carry2 = anc[6], anc[7]

    edges = [(0,1), (0,3), (0,4), (1,2), (2,3), (2,4), (2,5), (3,4), (3,5)]

    # Helper: controlled increment of the 3‑bit sum register
    # (add 1 to sum if control qubit is |1>)
    def controlled_increment(ctrl, sum0, sum1, sum2, t1, t2):
        # compute C1 = ctrl AND sum0
        qc.ccx(ctrl, sum0, t1)
        # compute C2 = t1 AND sum1
        qc.ccx(t1, sum1, t2)
        # update sum2 with C2
        qc.cx(t2, sum2)
        # uncompute C2 (using current sum1, still unchanged)
        qc.ccx(t1, sum1, t2)
        # update sum1 with C1
        qc.cx(t1, sum1)
        # uncompute C1 (using current sum0, still unchanged)
        qc.ccx(ctrl, sum0, t1)
        # update sum0 with ctrl
        qc.cx(ctrl, sum0)

    # Helper: controlled decrement of the 3‑bit sum register
    # (reverse of the increment, so subtract 1 if control is |1>)
    def controlled_decrement(ctrl, sum0, sum1, sum2, t1, t2):
        # reverse of the increment sequence
        qc.ccx(ctrl, sum0, t1)
        qc.ccx(t1, sum1, t2)
        qc.cx(t2, sum2)
        qc.ccx(t1, sum1, t2)
        qc.cx(t1, sum1)
        qc.ccx(ctrl, sum0, t1)
        qc.cx(ctrl, sum0)

    # (1 iff both u and v are 0) into edge_tmp, then CNOT it into bad.
    # After the operation edge_tmp and edge_and are returned to |0>.
    def process_edge(u, v, set_flag=True):

        qc.cx(p[v], edge_tmp)
        # compute x_u AND x_v into edge_and

        qc.cx(edge_and, edge_tmp)

        else:

        qc.cx(p[v], edge_tmp)     # back to x_u only

    for u, v in reversed(edges):
        process_edge(u, v, set_flag=False)

def build_oracle(qc: QuantumCircuit, problem_qubits: list[int],

        apply_x_for_offset(o)

        (problem_qubits[2], problem_qubits[3], problem_qubits[4]),  # offset 2
        (problem_qubits[3], problem_qubits[4], problem_qubits[5]),  # offset 3
        (problem_qubits[4], problem_qubits[5], problem_qubits[6]),  # offset 4
        (problem_qubits[5], problem_qubits[6], problem_qubits[7]),  # offset 5
    ]

    pattern = "10011" (no wildcards) of length 5 over a text of 8 bits.
    f(x) = 1 iff the pattern appears as a contiguous substring at some offset o in 0..3.
    """

        text_qubits = [problem_qubits[o + i] for i in range(5)]

        # Apply X on qubits that should be 0 (so that control checks |1>)
        for i, q in enumerate(text_qubits):
            if pattern[i] == 0:
                qc.x(q)

        # Multi‑controlled NOT: flip ancilla if all five conditions hold
        qc.mcx(text_qubits, ancilla_qubits[o], mode='noancilla')

        # Restore the problem qubits
        for i, q in enumerate(text_qubits):
            if pattern[i] == 0:
                qc.x(q)

    # ---- 2. Phase flip if ANY offset matches (OR of match qubits) ----
    # Complement the match ancillas
    for anc in ancilla_qubits:

    qc.x(tmp)                                        # tmp = OR

    Implements a phase oracle for the pattern matching problem:
    text s of length 8 (s0..s7 on problem_qubits), pattern "1101"
    (no wildcards) of length 4, marks states where the pattern appears
    as a contiguous substring at any offset 0..4.

    p = problem_qubits

    tmp1 = anc[1]
    tmp2 = anc[2]
    tmp3 = anc[3]

        """Compute the match condition for offset `offset` into `target`.
        Pattern bit: 1, 1, 0, 1  (indices 0..3)

        # it will be undone by the uncompute call (which is identical).

        """Exactly the same as compute_match because the operation is self‑inverse."""
        compute_match(offset, target)

    def or_forward(a: int, b: int, c: int) -> None:
        """Reversible OR: c = a OR b, assuming c starts as 0.
        Leaves a, b unchanged.
        """
        qc.cx(a, c)
        qc.cx(b, c)
        qc.ccx(a, b, c)

    def or_reverse(a: int, b: int, c: int) -> None:
        """Inverse of or_forward: restores c to 0 and leaves a,b unchanged."""

        qc.cx(b, c)
        qc.cx(a, c)

    compute_match(1, tmp2)                # m1 into tmp2

    # Patter: "1101" (fixed, no wildcards)

    n_problem = 8
    n_pattern = 4
    n_offsets = n_problem - n_pattern + 1  # 5

    # Helper: compute condition for offset o into target ancilla t.
    # Uses a2, a3 as scratch.  Applies X on relevant problem qubits for 0 bits.
    def compute_condition(o: int, target: int):
        # Build 4-controlled X (TOFFOLI chain) with controls on
        # problem_qubits[o+i] (possibly flipped if pattern[i]==0).
        # Use 2 ancillas (a2, a3) as per standard decomposition.
        # (All ancillas start 0.)
        ctrl1 = problem_qubits[o]
        ctrl2 = problem_qubits[o+1]
        ctrl3 = problem_qubits[o+2]
        ctrl4 = problem_qubits[o+3]

        # Apply X on controls for pattern bits that are 0
        if pattern[0] == 0:

        if pattern[1] == 0:

        if pattern[2] == 0:

        if pattern[3] == 0:
            qc.x(ctrl4)

        # step1: first two controls

        # step2: next two controls
        qc.ccx(ctrl3, ctrl4, a3)

        if pattern[1] == 0:

from qiskit import QuantumCircuit

def build_oracle(qc: QuantumCircuit, problem_qubits: list[int],
                 ancilla_qubits: list[int]) -> None:
    """
    Grover oracle for the problem:
      - 3-SAT clauses:
        (¬x2 ∨ x3 ∨ x4)
        (x1 ∨ ¬x3 ∨ x5)
        (x1 ∨ ¬x3 ∨ x6)
        (x1 ∨ x3 ∨ ¬x4)
      - Cardinality: number of true variables ≤ 5

    Uses 7 ancilla qubits. Applies a diagonal phase -1 to states that satisfy
    both constraints. All ancillas are returned to |0>.
    """
    # Assign ancilla roles
    g = ancilla_qubits[0]      # SAT flag (1 iff all clauses true)
    h = ancilla_qubits[1]      # sum > 5 flag (1 iff sum ≥ 6)
    flag = ancilla_qubits[2]   # final combined flag (1 iff solution)
    scratch_c = ancilla_qubits[3]  # scratch for clause computations
    scratch_s = ancilla_qubits[4]  # scratch for sum term computations
    # ancilla_qubits[5], [6] left unused (stay |0>)

    # --- 3-SAT clauses ---
    # Each clause false condition expressed as a 3‑controlled X.
    clauses = [
        ([problem_qubits[2], problem_qubits[3], problem_qubits[4]], '100'),
        ([problem_qubits[1], problem_qubits[3], problem_qubits[5]], '010'),
        ([problem_qubits[1], problem_qubits[3], problem_qubits[6]], '010'),
        ([problem_qubits[1], problem_qubits[3], problem_qubits[4]], '001')
    ]

    # --- Sum ≥ 6 terms (exactly one 0 or all 1) ---
    # All 7 ones
    sum_terms = [(problem_qubits[:], '1111111')]
    # Six ones (exactly one variable false)
    for i in range(7):
        ctrl = ['1'] * 7
        ctrl[i] = '0'
        sum_terms.append((problem_qubits[:], ''.join(ctrl)))

    # ---- Compute ----
    # 1) Compute g: start g=1, flip if any clause is false
    qc.x(g)
    for controls, state in clauses:
        qc.mcx(controls, scratch_c, ctrl_state=state, mode='noancilla')
        qc.cx(scratch_c, g)
        qc.mcx(controls, scratch_c, ctrl_state=state, mode='noancilla')

    # 2) Compute h: start h=0, flip for every term that makes sum ≥ 6
    for controls, state in sum_terms:
        qc.mcx(controls, scratch_s, ctrl_state=state, mode='noancilla')
        qc.cx(scratch_s, h)
        qc.mcx(controls, scratch_s, ctrl_state=state, mode='noancilla')

    # 3) Compute flag = g AND (not h)
    qc.x(h)
    qc.ccx(g, h, flag)
    qc.x(h)

    # ---- Phase ----
    qc.z(flag)

    # ---- Uncompute ----
    # Uncompute flag
    qc.x(h)
    qc.ccx(g, h, flag)
    qc.x(h)

    # Uncompute h (repeat sum terms loop)
    for controls, state in sum_terms:
        qc.mcx(controls, scratch_s, ctrl_state=state, mode='noancilla')

        qc.cx(scratch_c, g)
        qc.mcx(controls, scratch_c, ctrl_state=state, mode='noancilla')

    qc.x(g)

    patterns = list(itertools.combinations(range(8), 5))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # For each pattern of 5 ones, check if the input matches that pattern.
    # Accumulate the OR of all matches into anc[0] using a CNOT.
    for ones in patterns:
        zeros = [i for i in range(8) if i not in ones]
        # Invert the qubits that should be 0 (so that they become 1)
        for i in zeros:
            qc.x(prob[i])
        # Multi‑controlled X: target is anc[1], ancillas are anc[2..7]
        # This sets anc[1] to 1 iff all controls are 1 (after the inversions)
        qc.mcx(prob, anc[1], anc[2:8], mode='v-chain')
        # Accumulate: if pattern matches, flip anc[0] (the cardinality flag)
        qc.cx(anc[1], anc[0])
        # Uncompute the match (anc[1] and ancillas return to |0>)
        qc.mcx(prob, anc[1], anc[2:8], mode='v-chain')
        # Restore the problem qubits
        for i in zeros:
            qc.x(prob[i])

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

        [(1, False), (4, False), (5, False)]     # (¬x1 ∨ ¬x4 ∨ ¬x5)
    ]

    # Helper to apply/undo X for positive literals (where we need 0)
    def x_if_positive(lit):

        ([3, 5, 6], [False, False, True]),
        # (x0 OR x4 OR x6) -> false when x0=0, x4=0, x6=0
        ([0, 4, 6], [True, True, True])
    ]

def build_oracle(qc: QuantumCircuit, problem_qubits: list[int], ancilla_qubits: list[int]) -> None:
    # Unpack ancilla qubits based on roles
    # 0-3: sum register / clause sat (reused)
    # 4: cardinality flag
    # 5: overall flag / scratch for clause compute
    # 6,7: additional scratch for multi-controlled gates and card_flag

    card_flag = a[4]
    ov_flag = a[5]                 # overall flag, also used as scratch for clause compute
    scratch1 = a[6]               # scratch for card_flag and mcx
    scratch2 = a[7]               # scratch for card_flag and mcx

    # ---------- Step 1: Compute sum into s ----------
    def controlled_increment(control):
        """Increment the 4-bit register s by 1 if control is 1."""
        qc.cx(control, s[0])
        # Use available ancillas: card_flag, ov_flag, scratch1, scratch2 are free during sum computation
        anc_list = [card_flag, ov_flag, scratch1, scratch2]
        # k=1: controls [control, s[0]], target s[1]
        qc.mcx([control, s[0]], s[1], ancilla_qubits=anc_list)
        # k=2: controls [control, s[0], s[1]], target s[2]
        qc.mcx([control, s[0], s[1]], s[2], ancilla_qubits=anc_list)
        # k=3: controls [control, s[0], s[1], s[2]], target s[3]
        qc.mcx([control, s[0], s[1], s[2]], s[3], ancilla_qubits=anc_list)

    # Forward sum: process all problem qubits
    for p in problem_qubits:
        controlled_increment(p)

    # ---------- Step 2: Compute cardinality flag (>=5) ----------
    # card_flag = s3 OR (s2 AND (s1 OR s0))
    # Use scratch1, scratch2, ov_flag as temporary ancillas (ov_flag is free here)
    temp1 = scratch1   # will hold s1 OR s0
    temp2 = scratch2   # will hold s2 AND temp1
    temp3 = ov_flag    # will hold NOT s3 for computing OR

    # Compute temp1 = s1 OR s0
    # Using: NOT(s1) AND NOT(s0) -> NOT give OR
    qc.x(s[1]); qc.x(s[0])
    qc.ccx(s[1], s[0], temp1)
    qc.x(s[1]); qc.x(s[0])
    qc.x(temp1)       # now temp1 = s1 OR s0

    # Compute temp2 = s2 AND temp1
    qc.ccx(s[2], temp1, temp2)

    # method: card_flag = s3 XOR (temp2 AND NOT(s3))
    qc.cx(s[3], card_flag)        # if s3=1, set card_flag=1
    qc.x(temp3)
    qc.cx(s[3], temp3)            # temp3 = NOT s3
    qc.ccx(temp2, temp3, card_flag) # XOR (temp2 AND NOT(s3))
    # Now card_flag correctly set

    # For uncompute step we will keep temp1, temp2, temp3 as they are

    # ---------- Step 3: Uncompute sum (reverse increment) ----------
    # Process problem qubits in reverse order with inverse of increment
    # Since increment circuit is self-inverse (gates like CX, mcx are their own inverse),
    # we just apply the same circuits in reverse order of the problem qubits.
    for p in reversed(problem_qubits):
        controlled_increment(p)

    # We reuse the sum qubits s[0..3] as clause sat ancillas.

    # After each clause, scratch is returned to 0.

        qubits: list of three problem qubit indices
        signs: list of booleans (True = positive, False = negated)
        target: ancilla qubit index (one of s)
        Uses ov_flag as temporary scratch.
        Leaves target = 1 if clause satisfied, else 0.
        Uses and restores ov_flag.

        for q, sign in zip(qubits, signs):
            if not sign:
                qc.x(q)

        # Target is initially 0.
        qc.ccx(qubits[0], qubits[1], ov_flag)
        qc.ccx(ov_flag, qubits[2], target)
        qc.ccx(qubits[0], qubits[1], ov_flag)  # uncompute ov_flag
        # Invert to get clause_sat (if all literals false => target=0, need 1)
        qc.x(target)

            if not sign:
                qc.x(q)

    compute_clause(
        [problem_qubits[0], problem_qubits[2], problem_qubits[5]],
        [False, False, False],
        s[0]
    )
    # Clause 1: (NOT x3 OR NOT x4 OR x6)
    compute_clause(
        [problem_qubits[3], problem_qubits[4], problem_qubits[6]],
        [False, False, True],
        s[1]
    )
    # Clause 2: (NOT x0 OR x1 OR x5)
    compute_clause(
        [problem_qubits[0], problem_qubits[1], problem_qubits[5]],
        [False, True, True],
        s[2]

    compute_clause(
        [problem_qubits[4], problem_qubits[5], problem_qubits[7]],
        [True, False, True],

        target_qubit=ov_flag,
        ancilla_qubits=[scratch1, scratch2]
    )

    qc.z(ov_flag)

    qc.mcx(

        [True, False, True],

        [False, True, True],
        s[2]
    )
    # Clause 1
    compute_clause(
        [problem_qubits[3], problem_qubits[4], problem_qubits[6]],
        [False, False, True],
        s[1]
    )
    # Clause 0
    compute_clause(
        [problem_qubits[0], problem_qubits[2], problem_qubits[5]],
        [False, False, False],
        s[0]
    )

    # ---------- Step 9: Uncompute cardinality (recompute sum, revert card_flag, uncompute sum) ----------
    # Recompute sum forward (same as step 1)
    for p in problem_qubits:
        controlled_increment(p)

    # Uncompute card_flag (reverse of step 2)
    # Reverse order of gates in compute_card_flag
    # We have stored temp1=scratch1, temp2=scratch2, temp3=ov_flag (now 0, but will be used)

    #   CX(s3,card_flag), X(temp3), CX(s3,temp3), CCX(temp2,temp3,card_flag)
    # Reverse:

    # Actually after the uncompute of sum (step3) we reset sum register, but scratch qubits
    # were not touched since step2. So they still hold the values from step2.
    # So the reverse circuit correctly restores them to 0.
    qc.ccx(temp2, temp3, card_flag)    # note: temp3 = ov_flag
    qc.cx(s[3], temp3)
    qc.x(temp3)
    qc.cx(s[3], card_flag)
    qc.ccx(s[2], temp1, temp2)

import math
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit

def build_oracle(qc: QuantumCircuit, problem_qubits: list[int],
                 ancilla_qubits: list[int]) -> None:
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Variables
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # problem qubits: x0..x7
    p = problem_qubits

    # ancilla qubits (9 total)
    anc = ancilla_qubits
    # mapping:
    #   anc[0] : cardinality flag (F)
    #   anc[1..4] : count register (r0..r3, LSB first)
    #   anc[5..8] : temporary ancillas (carries, scratch)
    n_anc = 9
    # alias for clarity
    flag_card = anc[0]
    r0, r1, r2, r3 = anc[1], anc[2], anc[3], anc[4]
    tmp1 = anc[5]   # scratch for F computation, later for clauses etc.
    tmp2 = anc[6]   # scratch for 3-controlled NOT in increments, later for clauses
    tmp3 = anc[7]   # scratch for final combination
    tmp4 = anc[8]   # scratch for final combination

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Clauses
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # clauses: list of tuples (lit1, lit2, lit3), each literal is (var_idx, negated)
    # using indices 0..7 for x0..x7
    clauses = [
        [(0, True),  (3, False), (6, False)],   # (¬x0 OR x3 OR x6)
        [(0, True),  (2, True),  (5, False)],   # (¬x0 OR ¬x2 OR x5)
        [(2, False), (3, False), (6, False)],   # (x2 OR x3 OR x6)
        [(1, True),  (2, False), (4, True)],    # (¬x1 OR x2 OR ¬x4)
        [(0, True),  (4, True),  (5, True)]     # (¬x0 OR ¬x4 OR ¬x5)
    ]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Helper: controlled increment of the 4‑bit count register by 1
    #   control : the problem qubit that triggers the addition
    #   uses tmp1..tmp4 as carry ancillas
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def controlled_inc(ctrl):
        # carry chain with dedicated ancillas (tmp1..tmp4)
        # bit 0
        qc.cx(ctrl, tmp1)               # tmp1 = ctrl
        qc.ccx(tmp1, r0, tmp2)          # tmp2 = ctrl & r0
        qc.cx(tmp1, r0)                 # r0 ^= ctrl
        # bit 1
        qc.ccx(tmp2, r1, tmp3)          # tmp3 = carry0 & r1
        qc.cx(tmp2, r1)                 # r1 ^= carry0
        # bit 2
        qc.ccx(tmp3, r2, tmp4)          # tmp4 = carry1 & r2
        qc.cx(tmp3, r2)                 # r2 ^= carry1
        # bit 3
        qc.cx(tmp4, r3)                 # r3 ^= carry2
        # note: carry2 used for r3; overflow is ignored
        # now we must clean the carry ancillas (they are in a mixed state)
        # we will uncompute later, so we leave them as is for now.
        # (the uncompute will reverse all gates, restoring them to 0)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Step 1: Compute cardinality flag F = (sum ≤ 3)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1.a) Add each problem qubit to the count register
    for i in range(8):
        controlled_inc(p[i])

    # 1.b) Compute F = 1 if (r3 == 0 and r2 == 0)
    #      using tmp1 as scratch
    # Compute OR of r3 and r2 into tmp1, then F = NOT(tmp1)
    # OR = ¬(¬r3 ∧ ¬r2)
    qc.x(r3)
    qc.x(r2)
    qc.ccx(r3, r2, tmp1)   # tmp1 = ¬r3 ∧ ¬r2
    qc.x(tmp1)              # tmp1 = r3 ∨ r2
    qc.cx(tmp1, flag_card)  # flag_card = tmp1 (since init 0)
    # uncompute tmp1
    qc.x(tmp1)              # restore tmp1 = ¬r3 ∧ ¬r2
    qc.ccx(r3, r2, tmp1)    # clear tmp1
    qc.x(r2)
    qc.x(r3)
    # now flag_card = 1 iff sum ≤ 3 (i.e., r2=0 and r3=0)

    # 1.c) Uncompute the addition (reverse increments)
    for i in reversed(range(8)):
        # the reverse of controlled_inc is the same sequence with same controls
        controlled_inc(p[i])

    # after uncompute: count register back to 0, carry ancillas back to 0

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Step 2: Compute clause flags into anc[1..5]
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # We will compute clause j into anc[1+j] using tmp2 as scratch.
    clause_ancillas = [anc[1], anc[2], anc[3], anc[4], anc[5]]
    # note: anc[1..4] are free (0), anc[5] is free (we used anc[5] as clause_ancillas[4])
    # anc[6] (tmp2) used as scratch for clause AND

    for j, clause in enumerate(clauses):
        target = clause_ancillas[j]

        # apply X for negated literals
        for (var, neg) in clause:
            if neg:
                qc.x(p[var])

        # compute AND of the three (negated) literals into target using tmp2
        # step1: AND of first two into tmp2
        qc.ccx(p[clause[0][0]], p[clause[1][0]], tmp2)
        # step2: AND of tmp2 and third literal into target
        qc.ccx(tmp2, p[clause[2][0]], target)
        # uncompute tmp2
        qc.ccx(p[clause[0][0]], p[clause[1][0]], tmp2)

        # now target = 1 iff all three literals are false -> clause false
        # flip to get clause true:
        qc.x(target)

        # undo the X on problem qubits
        for (var, neg) in clause:
            if neg:
                qc.x(p[var])

    # after this clause_ancillas[0..4] hold clause satisfactions

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Step 3: Combine clause flags and cardinality flag into final flag
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # compute temp1 = AND(clause_ancillas[0], clause_ancillas[1], clause_ancillas[2]) into tmp1
    # compute temp2 = AND(clause_ancillas[3], clause_ancillas[4], flag_card) into tmp3
    # final = AND(temp1, temp2) into tmp4 (then phase flip)

    # temp1 on tmp1
    qc.ccx(clause_ancillas[0], clause_ancillas[1], tmp1)      # tmp1 = c0 & c1
    qc.ccx(tmp1, clause_ancillas[2], tmp1)                    # tmp1 = c0&c1&c2

    # temp2 on tmp3
    qc.ccx(clause_ancillas[3], clause_ancillas[4], tmp3)      # tmp3 = c3 & c4
    qc.ccx(tmp3, flag_card, tmp3)                              # tmp3 = c3&c4 & flag_card

    # final combine on tmp4
    qc.ccx(tmp1, tmp3, tmp4)                                   # tmp4 = temp1 & temp2

    # apply phase -1 if both conditions hold
    qc.z(tmp4)

    # uncompute in reverse order
    qc.ccx(tmp1, tmp3, tmp4)       # clear final
    qc.ccx(tmp3, flag_card, tmp3)  # clear temp2
    qc.ccx(clause_ancillas[3], clause_ancillas[4], tmp3)
    qc.ccx(tmp1, clause_ancillas[2], tmp1)  # clear temp1
    qc.ccx(clause_ancillas[0], clause_ancillas[1], tmp1)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Step 4: Uncompute clause flags
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # reverse step 2 in reverse order
    for j in reversed(range(5)):
        clause = clauses[j]
        target = clause_ancillas[j]

        # X for negated literals (same as compute)
        for (var, neg) in clause:
            if neg:
                qc.x(p[var])

        # undo the final X on target
        qc.x(target)

        # now uncompute the AND: reverse the Toffoli sequence
        # first recompute tmp2 (same as before)
        qc.ccx(p[clause[0][0]], p[clause[1][0]], tmp2)
        # then uncompute target
        qc.ccx(tmp2, p[clause[2][0]], target)
        # then uncompute tmp2
        qc.ccx(p[clause[0][0]], p[clause[1][0]], tmp2)

        # undo X on problem qubits
        for (var, neg) in clause:
            if neg:
                qc.x(p[var])

    # all clause ancillas are now 0, tmp2 is 0

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Step 5: Uncompute cardinality flag
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5.a) Uncompute F computation
    qc.cx(tmp1, flag_card)     # undo CNOT (tmp1 is 0, so it's fine)
    qc.x(tmp1)
    qc.ccx(r3, r2, tmp1)      # restore tmp1 = ¬r3 ∧ ¬r2
    qc.x(tmp1)                 # tmp1 = r3 ∨ r2
    qc.x(r2)
    qc.x(r3)
    # now flag_card = 0

    # 5.b) The count register and carry ancillas are already 0 from step 1 uncompute.
    #      All ancillas are 0 now.

from qiskit import QuantumCircuit

def build_oracle(qc: QuantumCircuit, problem_qubits: list[int],
                 ancilla_qubits: list[int]) -> None:
    # Naming ancillas for readability
    anc = ancilla_qubits
    # Final phase ancilla
    a0 = anc[0]
    # Helpers for combining conditions
    a1 = anc[1]
    a2 = anc[2]
    # Clause outputs (5 clauses)
    c1 = anc[3]
    c2 = anc[4]
    c3 = anc[5]
    c4 = anc[6]
    c5 = anc[7]
    # Cardinality result
    card = anc[8]

    # ---------- CARDINALITY (at most 3 true) ----------
    # Use anc[1..4] as 4‑bit sum register (LSB -> anc[1])
    s0, s1, s2, s3 = anc[1], anc[2], anc[3], anc[4]
    # Carry ancillas
    c_in = anc[5]
    c_out = anc[6]

    # Reset ancillas that will become dirty (already 0 at start)
    # We will build the sum by sequential addition of each problem qubit.
    # The addition circuit uses c_in and c_out as intermediate carries.
    # It modifies the sum register and the two carry ancillas.
    # At the end the final carry (c_out) will be 0 (max sum = 8).
    # The whole addition is reversible.

    # Helper: add one problem qubit (ctrl) to the 4‑bit register.
    def add_bit(ctrl, r0, r1, r2, r3):
        # first bit (LSB)
        qc.ccx(r0, ctrl, c_out)    # c_out = r0 & ctrl
        qc.cx(ctrl, r0)            # r0 ^= ctrl
        # second bit
        qc.ccx(r1, c_out, c_in)    # c_in = r1 & c_out
        qc.cx(c_out, r1)           # r1 ^= c_out
        # third bit
        qc.ccx(r2, c_in, c_out)    # c_out = r2 & c_in
        qc.cx(c_in, r2)            # r2 ^= c_in
        # fourth bit (most significant)
        qc.ccx(r3, c_out, c_in)    # c_in = r3 & c_out
        qc.cx(c_out, r3)           # r3 ^= c_out

    # Add all 8 problem qubits to the sum register
    for pb in problem_qubits:
        add_bit(pb, s0, s1, s2, s3)
        # After the last addition, c_in holds the final carry (0),
        # but we will uncompute everything later, so it's fine.

    # Now anc[1..4] hold the total number of true variables.
    # Condition: sum <= 3  <=>  (s2 == 0 and s3 == 0)
    qc.x(s2)
    qc.x(s3)
    qc.ccx(s2, s3, card)   # card = 1 iff (s2==0 and s3==0)
    qc.x(s2)
    qc.x(s3)

    # ---------- CLAUSE COMPUTATIONS ----------
    # Clause 1: (NOT x0 OR x3 OR x6)
    # clause false iff (x0=1, x3=0, x6=0)
    # We set c1 = 1 if clause true.
    p0, p3, p6 = problem_qubits[0], problem_qubits[3], problem_qubits[6]
    qc.x(p3)
    qc.x(p6)
    qc.ccx(p0, p3, p6, c1)   # c1 = 1 if clause false
    qc.x(p3)
    qc.x(p6)
    qc.x(c1)                 # now c1 = 1 if clause true

    # Clause 2: (NOT x0 OR NOT x2 OR x5)
    # false iff (x0=1, x2=1, x5=0)
    p2, p5 = problem_qubits[2], problem_qubits[5]
    qc.x(p5)                 # flip x5
    qc.ccx(problem_qubits[0], p2, p5, c2)
    qc.x(p5)

    - 5 3-SAT clauses (see problem statement)
    - Cardinality constraint: exactly 5 out of 8 variables are True.

    t_clause = ancilla_qubits[1]      # temporary for clause unsatisfied

    sum2 = ancilla_qubits[5]
    sum3 = ancilla_qubits[6]   # MSB

    car1 = ancilla_qubits[8]   # temporary carry 1

        qc.ccx(temp_bit, flag, scratch)   # scratch = temp_bit & flag
        qc.cx(scratch, flag)              # flag ^= scratch  (flag becomes 0 if scratch=1)
        qc.ccx(temp_bit, flag, scratch)   # uncompute scratch

        [(problem_qubits[1], False), (problem_qubits[5], True), (problem_qubits[6], True)],

        [(problem_qubits[0], False), (problem_qubits[3], False), (problem_qubits[6], True)],
